title: No Verified Incident Supports Dog-Trade Defenses
excerpt: No police record, court judgment, seizure, or health alert appears in supplied material. Claims about farms, theft, and safety need public evidence before public trust.
body_html:
No verified police seizure, court conviction, intercepted shipment, or emergency health alert appears in the material available for this dispatch. That absence blocks honest claims about a specific stolen companion, poison-bait incident, or contaminated consignment. It does not make dog-trade defenses credible. It means public reporting must start with records, not invention.

Myths need evidence

“Tradition” cannot answer basic accountability questions: Where were animals sourced? Were ownership records checked? Were veterinary inspections completed? Were quarantine rules followed? “Farm-raised” cannot be treated as fact without licensing, traceability, transport, and inspection records. No such records were supplied here. No responsible campaign should declare that every animal enters trade through theft, just as no operator should receive public trust without proof.

Biosecurity cannot run on claims

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply-chain failures remain separate risks; neither permits unsupported causal claims. WHO guidance sets medical facts. Records must establish trade-chain facts.

Vietnamese communities deserve protection

Families, pet owners, veterinarians, and local authorities need transparent enforcement against illegal transport, quarantine evasion, poisoning, and theft where documented. They also need policy that closes regulatory gaps without blaming communities or treating lawful conduct as criminal.

SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
